title: NEO: Saving GPU Memory Crisis with CPU Offloading for Online LLM Inference
technique: offload part of decode attention compute and KV cache to host CPU; asymmetric GPU-CPU pipelining with two sub-batches; load-aware scheduling of offload decisions

optimized_metrics.evidence: This paper aims to achieve higher throughput for online LLM inference without compromising accuracy or latency in a cost-efficient way
NEO achieves up to 7.5×, 26%, and 14% higher throughput compared to GPU-only approach on T4, A10G, and H100 GPUs, respectively, while maintaining the same latency

headline_claim.text: NEO achieves up to 7.5×, 26%, and 14% higher throughput compared to GPU-only approach on T4, A10G, and H100 GPUs, respectively, while maintaining the same latency; with more powerful CPUs, NEO achieves up to 79.3% throughput gain on A10G GPU.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 6 average per-token latency vs request rate
throughput at fixed latency (1-2 s per token) from load-latency curves; Figs 8-10 relative throughput

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For each request, we compute its per-token latency by dividing its full latency by its output token number, and then we take the average among all requests.
metric_definitions.notes: full request latency / output tokens, i.e. normalized latency, mean over requests; not TPOT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: NEO achieves 14.3% higher throughput on H100 (at 2 sec latency), 6.40% higher on A10G (at 2 sec latency), and 563% higher on T4 (at 1 sec latency).
metric_definitions.notes: throughput read off load-latency curve at a latency bound; units req/s vs tokens/s not stated precisely

slo_spec: no formal SLO; throughput compared at fixed average per-token latency (1 or 2 s)
load_regime: request-rate sweep with Poisson arrivals; also fixed-length offline-style throughput tests (§5.4)
tradeoff_acknowledged: at higher request rates NEO latency is slightly higher than vLLM (less engineering optimization, overhead from offloading attempts); with short sequences NEO may perform slightly worse
hardware: AWS g4 (T4), g5 (A10G), HGX 2xH100 (single NUMA node)
workloads: Azure code (AC) trace-derived dataset, OpenAI summarization; fixed-length synthetic
extractor_notes: Objective is throughput subject to unchanged latency (constraint expressed as average normalized latency curve). Title says 'online' inference but no SLO.
